messages.author: 34338e949733aa9b
messages.subject: Theophylline Example Using STAN
parts:
Dear STAN team,

I am recently learning to use STAN. There is a classic Theophylline example in NONMEM, so I just want to redo it in STAN. But a couple of problems arise, so I really need your help.

Background:
We have 12 subjects, each with 11 observations.
theta1 ,theta2, theta3 are fixed effects.
eta1, eta2, eta3 are random effects with mean 0.
sigma is the error term and Omega is the covariance matrix.

I want to have the estimates of 3 fixed effects, 1 error term and 6 covariance parameters and code are in newtest.stan.

Problems are:
1. If I specify Omega as cov_matrix[3], I got 3 kinds of the messages: (1) Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Location parameter is inf:0, but must be finite! (2) Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_prec_log(d): LDLT_Factor of precision parameterunderlying matrix is not positive definite. LDLT_Factor of precision parameterlast conditional variance is 180.4616997051736. and (3) Optimization terminated with error:  Line search failed to achieve a sufficient decrease, no more progress can be made
The result in output.csv is not in accordance with NONMEM output

2. If I specify Omega as matrix[3,3], I got the message: Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_prec_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Precision matrixPrecision matrix is not symmetric. Precision matrix[1,2] is -14.756310354014762:0, but Precision matrix[2,1] element is -14.7563:0
Optimization terminated normally:  Convergence detected: change in objective function was below tolerance
Even though it is converged, but result in output.csv is not in accordance with NONMEM output

Question:
Did I make some mistakes or Could you please give me some suggestions?

Thank you so much!

Bests,
Fei

PS: theo5.nmctl.txt is the NONMEM file and theo5.ext.txt is the NONMEM output

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Theophylline Example Using STAN
parts:
Sorry for taking so long to respond. I just found a bunch of
e-mails I missed last week when I was traveling.

See answers inline.

On Jun 17, 2014, at 10:41 AM, Fei He <hefeif...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear STAN team,
>
> I am recently learning to use STAN. There is a classic Theophylline example in NONMEM, so I just want to redo it in STAN. But a couple of problems arise, so I really need your help.

Great --- we'd love to get some of those examples working.

We should be rolling out a diff-eq solvers before the end of
this year.

> Background:
> We have 12 subjects, each with 11 observations.
> theta1 ,theta2, theta3 are fixed effects.
> eta1, eta2, eta3 are random effects with mean 0.
> sigma is the error term and Omega is the covariance matrix.
>
> I want to have the estimates of 3 fixed effects, 1 error term and 6 covariance parameters and code are in newtest.stan.
>
> Problems are:
> 1. If I specify Omega as cov_matrix[3], I got 3 kinds of the messages: (1) Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Location parameter is inf:0, but must be finite! (2) Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_prec_log(d): LDLT_Factor of precision parameterunderlying matrix is not positive definite. LDLT_Factor of precision parameterlast conditional variance is 180.4616997051736. and

These first two aren't necessarily a problem if they don't persist across
iterations.
> (3) Optimization terminated with error: Line search failed to achieve a sufficient decrease, no more progress can be made
This is more of a problem.
> The result in output.csv is not in accordance with NONMEM output

NONMEM does marginal maximum likelihood for random effects, which is
not what Stan does (at least not yet, though it's in the works).
Right now, we have only a simple (penalized) maximum likelihood estimator.

What that's likely to do in practice for hierarchical models is
drive the hierarchical variance to 0, because it drives up the likelihood.

>
> 2. If I specify Omega as matrix[3,3], I got the message: Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_prec_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Precision matrixPrecision matrix is not symmetric. Precision matrix[1,2] is -14.756310354014762:0, but Precision matrix[2,1] element is -14.7563:0

We're hoping to fix this issue with Stan 2.4 by only using the
lower triangular portion and thus enforcing symmetry in the
function itself.

> Optimization terminated normally: Convergence detected: change in objective function was below tolerance

> Even though it is converged, but result in output.csv is not in accordance with NONMEM output

See above. If you have a covariance matrix parameter, as Omega is,
you really need to declare it as such. If it's a generated quantity or
transformed parameter, it's not a big deal, as uses of it will
enforce its structure.

> Question:
> Did I make some mistakes or Could you please give me some suggestions?

I suspect the problem here is really trying to apply maximum likelihood
in a situation where you need marginal maximum likelihood (integrates out
the low-level parameters, optimizes the marginal of the high-level
parameter, then uses those to estimate low-level parameters).

You could try running with NUTS in sampling mode. That can deal
with hierarchical models. It'll be slower, but should work.

We'd also recommend using unconstrained parameters rather than putting
upper and lower bounds on them; if you use bounded parameters, you
should be careful you're not getting estimates up against a boundary.

Also, if Omega is truly a covariance matrix (and not a precision matrix),
then you should use multi_normal, not multi_normal_prec. Sorry for the
confusion with the variable type being named cov_matrix --- it should
just be spd_matrix, for symmetric-positive-definite matrix. We're going
to change it in the future and deprecate the "cov_matrix" type (and
then eventually get rid of it).

- Bob

>
> Thank you so much!
>
> Bests,
> Fei
